reason: Mixed and unclear: 'cellular surface' of bulbils suggests a net of cell outlines (areolate), while 'formées de cellules allongées' describes the cells themselves, not a quality of the scale. No single reading holds across the floras.

'Pedicel elongating considerably in fruit' and 'inflorescence much elongating in fruit' describe growth that goes on after flowering, which is accrescent. Other uses ('teeth elongating to bristles', 'veins elongating to apex') are not a quality and stay unresolved.

label: moss-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a whole plant or shoot by virtue of its being small, with slender stems densely covered by minute crowded leaves, resembling a moss.
reason: A habit comparison used across six floras in English and French, in the same way as FLOPO:0991039 palm-like. No PATO or FLOPO term covers it.
'Midrib not projecting' and 'connective not projecting' mean not extending above or beyond a surface or boundary, the negation of PATO:0001598 protruding.

'Cloisonnées' anthers, locules and stems are divided by septa (PO:0000030, with ovary, fruit and anther septum as children). 'Hypanthium: cloisons de 1–1,5 mm' takes the septum as bearer of a measurement.

target: new: quality of a part named in the word (pubescent PATO_0000455 + trichome PO_0000282 brown PATO_0000952)
reason: Two statements in one word: the bearer is pubescent and its hairs are brown. The colour belongs to the hairs, not the bearer (as recorded for 'rust' in flora_union_pairs).
Strap-like = shaped like a narrow band, which is PATO:0002430 (as with the rule for ligulate).
Conglomerate inflorescences and bracts are crowded into a mass: PATO:0001629 aggregated (EXACT synonyms clumped, clustered).

Subrotundate petals, stipules and leaves are nearly round in outline: PATO:0002397 subcircular (RELATED synonym round). 'Apice subrotundatis' (a nearly rounded apex) is better read as PATO:0001935 obtuse.
A ratio of width to height greater than 1, stated for cells, arils and fruits. It is not a shape term, although for fruits it is close to FLOPO:0991103 depressed.
Floras use it to set green leaves, stems and spores against achlorophyllous (mycoheterotrophic or parasitic) ones. Green is the nearest existing term; PATO has no 'photosynthetic' quality.

target: new: quality of a part named in the word (striped: banded PATO_0001946 / streaked FLOPO:0991206 + stripe purple PATO_0000951)
reason: Two values in one word: a striped colour pattern, and the colour of the stripes. 'With purple stripes' shows that the colour belongs to the stripes, not the whole corolla or calyx.
Keel-like sepals, petals and midribs are keel-shaped, as in the rules for keeled and carinate.

It states that a neck is absent, but 'neck' was rejected as a generic part with no class (only the moss sporangium base PO_0030040 has 'neck' as a synonym). It cannot be grounded for ovaries, fruits and bulbs.

label: bud-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a bud: small, compact and ovoid, with closely overlapping scales or bracts.
reason: Used across six floras for male strobili, male inflorescences and short branches, much like bract-like FLOPO:0991200. No existing term says 'resembling a bud'.

target: new: compound of two shape values (cylindrical PATO_0001873 + elliptic PATO_0000947); continuum in docs/annotation-context-patterns.md section 2
reason: A hyphenated compound of two existing values (a shape between cylindrical and ellipsoid). It should be split into its two values, not given its own term.
'Sub-' + spatulate = approximately spatulate, handled like 'suborbicular' with value_qualifier approximately.
The negation of keeled, which maps to PATO:0002522 keel-shaped.

target: new: compound of two shape values (elliptic PATO_0000947 + oblanceolate PATO_0002330); continuum in docs/annotation-context-patterns.md section 2
reason: A hyphenated compound of two existing outline values, to be split rather than given its own term.
Intricate branches and branchlets are entwined and hard to separate: PATO:0001846 tangled. 'Seed intriquées' is unclear and may be left unresolved.

label: orthotropous
definition: An orientation quality inhering in an ovule by virtue of its being straight and erect on its funicle, with the micropyle at the end opposite the point of attachment.
reason: A standard botanical ovule type with no PATO or FLOPO term. Anatropous and campylotropous would be its siblings; an 'orthotropous embryo' uses the same sense.
Resin dots are small resin-secreting glands on the surface, which is what gland-dotted covers (dots that are glands). 'Resinous' stays FLOPO:0991075.
'Sharply' only stresses the angle; the value is the botanical acute apex or base.

Clinging stems and plants grow upwards by clinging to a support, which is in the definition of climbing. 'Leaf: embrassant la tige' is clasping (PATO:0104363), and 'bract: accrochantes' is better read as hooked.
PATO:0002215 falciform has 'hooked', 'uncinate' and 'unciform' as EXACT synonyms.
Monothecous = an anther with one theca: a count of parts whose part is named in the word ('à une seule thèque').
Layered bark and crowns with tiers of branches show a layered configuration: PATO:0002068 stratified.

target: new: quality of a part named in the word (petiolule PO_0020050 decreased length PATO_0000574)
reason: Petiolulate is already petiolule present (rule C209). 'Short' is the length of the petiolule, not of the leaflet, so it needs the part named in the word as bearer.

Most rows say the fruit is a utricle ('fruits thus utricles', 'Utricle 2-3 mm diam.'), a fruit type that PO has as PO:0030097. Utriculate pitchers and rosettes (bladder-like) are a minority, nearest to FLOPO:0991140 saccate.
Spindly plants and stems are long and thin for their height: PATO:0002212 slender (RELATED synonym gracile).
